raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

In deterministic mode, a token's routed experts must not depend on the server start or on the other tokens in the batch. The routing functions in `layers/moe/topk.py` are wrapped in `torch.compile`. Inductor tunes the generated kernels (block sizes, reduction splits) by timing them on first use, so the summation order of the routing scores can differ between server starts and batch shapes. With it, the selected experts can differ too. On MI350X this made DeepSeek-V2-Lite pass the deterministic checks on some server starts and fail on others (see below). This PR runs these routing functions eagerly in batch-invariant mode and keeps them compiled in normal mode.

**Scope.** The change applies on every platform, to models whose routing reaches these Python functions:
- DeepSeek-V2-style softmax grouped top-k (`grouped_topk_gpu`), for example DeepSeek-V2 / V2-Lite;
- Kimi K2-style biased top-k (`kimi_k2_biased_topk_impl`, `biased_topk_impl`);
- DeepSeek-V3-style sigmoid + correction-bias grouped top-k (`biased_grouped_topk_impl`, used for example by DeepSeek-V3/R1, Kimi-K3 and GLM-4.5), when no fused routing kernel takes over.

Where a fused kernel runs instead, this PR does not change anything. Examples:
- `fused_topk_deepseek` and `moe_fused_gate` on CUDA;
- AITER's routing kernel on ROCm with `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1`, which is the case for DeepSeek-V3-style routing on MI300/MI350.

DeepSeek-V4 cannot run in deterministic mode yet (its attention backend is refused), so it is not covered here.

The failure was reproduced and the fix validated end to end on DeepSeek-V2-Lite. The other models above are listed because they call these functions, not as end-to-end runs.

## Modifications

- `layers/moe/topk.py`: the five `torch.compile`'d routing functions (`grouped_topk_gpu`, `kimi_k2_biased_topk_impl`, `biased_topk_impl`, `biased_grouped_topk_impl`, `_biased_grouped_topk_postprocess`) are compiled through a small decorator, `_compile_unless_batch_invariant`, which keeps the compiled function for normal mode and calls the original one when batch-invariant mode is on. The compile options are unchanged.
- New CPU unit test `test/registered/unit/layers/moe/test_topk_batch_invariant_eager.py`: the five functions are wrapped; in batch-invariant mode the compiled function is never called and the result equals the eager function bit for bit; in normal mode the compiled function is used.
- Unchanged: normal mode (still compiled); routing paths that use fused kernels (`moe_fused_gate`, AITER) instead of these functions.

## Accuracy Tests

MI350X, ROCm 7.2.4, `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.22-rocm724-mi35x-20261021`, DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat, deterministic mode (`--enable-deterministic-inference --attention-backend triton`, AITER on and off, together with the other open MI350X deterministic-mode PRs), fresh servers, `python3 -m sglang.test.test_deterministic --test-mode single --n-trials 50` plus a bitwise batch-size check (the same prompt in batches of 1 to 50, 1,275 responses, token IDs and logprobs compared exactly with the batch-size-1 response):

| setup | servers that pass |
| --- | --- |
| before, TP1 (AITER on / off) | 4 of 6 |
| before, TP2 (AITER on / off, custom or RCCL all-reduce, with or without CUDA graphs) | 3 of 12 |
| `torch.compile` disabled entirely (`TORCHDYNAMO_DISABLE=1`), TP1 / TP2 | 12 of 12 / 3 of 3 |
| only these routing functions uncompiled, TP1 / TP2 | 8 of 8 / 3 of 3 |
| this branch, TP1 / TP2 | 8 of 8 / 8 of 8 |

Failing servers: `single` 2 outputs and bitwise 1 / 1,275 (AITER on), or identical tokens but log-probabilities 1 / 1,275 (AITER off); passing servers: 1 output and 1,275 / 1,275.

GSM8K (sgl-eval 0.1.2, `--temperature 0 --max-tokens 2048`, all 1,319 questions, DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat TP1, same image): 59.97% in deterministic mode with this change (before: 60.12% deterministic, 60.12% normal mode).

Unit tests (MI350X image): `python3 -m pytest -q test/registered/unit/layers/moe/test_topk_batch_invariant_eager.py`: 3 passed.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Normal mode is unchanged (the routing stays compiled). Deterministic mode, DeepSeek-V2-Lite TP1, `python3 -m sglang.benchmark.serving --backend sglang --dataset-name random --random-range-ratio 1.0 --request-rate inf`, output tok/s, two rounds:

| | 1k in / 1k out, 256 prompts | 8k in / 1k out, 128 prompts |
| --- | --- | --- |
| before (compiled routing) | 7,282 / 7,276 | 1,453 / 1,454 |
| routing uncompiled | 7,062 / 7,123 (-2.5%) | 1,443 / 1,443 (-0.7%) |

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

Thanks @rkarhila-amd !

On the models: only DeepSeek-V2-Lite was tested. It is the model where the failure showed up on MI350X (compiled grouped top-k gave a batch-dependent result on 1/3 to 2/3 of server starts), and it fits on one GPU. DeepSeek V3 and Kimi K2 in the description are the architectures that call these functions, not runs. I'll reword it so that's clear.

- **Kimi-K3:** it uses the same routing family (`TopK` with grouped top-k, sigmoid scoring and a correction bias), so it goes through `biased_grouped_topk_gpu`.
  - **ROCm with AITER on:** that function dispatches to AITER's routing kernel, not the compiled `biased_grouped_topk_impl`, so this PR doesn't change that path. AITER's kernel routes each token independently, but I haven't verified it end to end on K3.
  - **AITER off, and the platforms that fall back to the compiled function:** this PR applies.
- **DeepSeek-V4:** deterministic mode currently refuses its attention backend, so it can't run deterministic yet. Its routing needs its own check once it can.

To cover the most used model in this family, I'm checking DeepSeek-V3's router directly. I'll add the results here.

On style, I agree it isn't pretty. I kept the existing `torch.compile(..., disable=_is_npu)` arguments unchanged and only routed them through one decorator, so normal mode compiles exactly as before.

@rkarhila-amd Follow-up on the newer architectures: I checked DeepSeek-V3's router on its own. The config is 256 experts, 8 groups, top-4 groups, top-8, sigmoid + correction bias, renormalized, routed scaling 2.5. I routed the same 512 tokens in batches of 1 to 512 (bitwise per token), in 8 fresh processes each with AITER on and off, on MI350X:

| implementation | batch-size mismatches | same result in every process |
| --- | --- | --- |
| compiled `biased_grouped_topk_impl` (main) | 0 | yes (16/16) |
| eager (this PR, deterministic mode) | 0 | yes (16/16) |
| `biased_grouped_topk_gpu` with AITER on (AITER's routing kernel) | 0 | yes (8/8) |
| `biased_grouped_topk_gpu` with AITER off (falls back to the compiled function) | 0 | yes (8/8) |

So DeepSeek-V3-style routing did not show the problem here. The AITER path that ROCm uses is batch-invariant and stable across processes, and so was the compiled fallback in this test. Eager and compiled give slightly different bits (different rounding), but each is stable. The variance this PR fixes was seen on DeepSeek-V2-Lite's softmax `grouped_topk_gpu` path. For DeepSeek-V3-style models the PR is a safeguard: in deterministic mode the fallback no longer depends on Inductor's autotuning at all.

Looks ugly and hacky but ok. 

Having multiple decorators calls have a "disable=_is_npu" is setting a low standard anyway.

Description mentions having been tested on ds v2 and kimi k-2. Why so old? Is this relevant for Kimi-K3 and DS4?

detail.title: [Fix] deterministic: Run the MoE routing functions eagerly in batch-invariant mode

files.patch:
@@ -14,6 +14,7 @@
 
 from __future__ import annotations
 
+import functools
 import logging
 import math
 from dataclasses import dataclass, field
@@ -91,6 +92,7 @@ def routing(
 
 from sglang.kernels.fused_op import BaseFusedOp
 from sglang.kernels.ops.moe.dsv4 import mask_topk_ids
+from sglang.srt.batch_invariant_ops import is_batch_invariant_mode_enabled
 from sglang.srt.distributed.device_communicators.pynccl_allocator import (
     use_symmetric_memory,
 )
@@ -146,6 +148,31 @@ def routing(
 _use_aiter = get_bool_env_var("SGLANG_USE_AITER") and _is_hip
 _is_musa = is_musa()
 
+
+def _compile_unless_batch_invariant(**compile_kwargs):
+    """torch.compile a routing function, but run it eagerly in batch-invariant mode.
+
+    Inductor tunes the generated kernels (block sizes, reduction splits) by timing
+    on first use, so the summation order of the routing scores, and with it the
+    selected experts, can differ between server starts and with the batch.
+    Deterministic inference needs the eager kernels, whose order is fixed.
+    """
+
+    def decorator(fn):
+        compiled = torch.compile(fn, **compile_kwargs)
+
+        @functools.wraps(fn)
+        def wrapper(*args, **kwargs):
+            if is_batch_invariant_mode_enabled():
+                return fn(*args, **kwargs)
+            return wrapper.compiled(*args, **kwargs)
+
+        wrapper.compiled = compiled
+        return wrapper
+
+    return decorator
+
+
 # Epsilon added to the top-k weight sum before renormalization, matching the
 # DeepSeek reference gate (modeling_deepseek.py: `topk_weight.sum(...) + 1e-20`)
 # and flashinfer's trtllm routing kernels (mSumEpsilon). With sigmoid scoring
@@ -1380,7 +1407,9 @@ def fused_topk(
 
 
 # This is used by the Deepseek V2/V3/R1 series models
-@torch.compile(dynamic=True, backend=get_compiler_backend(), disable=_is_npu)
+@_compile_unless_batch_invariant(
+    dynamic=True, backend=get_compiler_backend(), disable=_is_npu
+)
 def grouped_topk_gpu(
     hidden_states: torch.Tensor,
     gating_output: torch.Tensor,
@@ -1538,7 +1567,9 @@ def grouped_topk_xpu(
     )
 
 
-@torch.compile(dynamic=True, backend=get_compiler_backend(), disable=_is_npu)
+@_compile_unless_batch_invariant(
+    dynamic=True, backend=get_compiler_backend(), disable=_is_npu
+)
 def kimi_k2_biased_topk_impl(
     hidden_states: torch.Tensor,
     gating_output: torch.Tensor,
@@ -1579,7 +1610,9 @@ def kimi_k2_biased_topk_impl(
     return topk_weights, topk_ids
 
 
-@torch.compile(dynamic=True, backend=get_compiler_backend(), disable=_is_npu)
+@_compile_unless_batch_invariant(
+    dynamic=True, backend=get_compiler_backend(), disable=_is_npu
+)
 def biased_topk_impl(
     hidden_states: torch.Tensor,
     gating_output: torch.Tensor,
@@ -1776,7 +1809,9 @@ def biased_topk_xpu(
     return output, indices
 
 
-@torch.compile(dynamic=True, backend=get_compiler_backend(), disable=_is_npu)
+@_compile_unless_batch_invariant(
+    dynamic=True, backend=get_compiler_backend(), disable=_is_npu
+)
 def biased_grouped_topk_impl(
     hidden_states: torch.Tensor,
     gating_output: torch.Tensor,
@@ -1952,7 +1987,7 @@ def _zero_topk_weights_padded_region(
     topk_weights[indices >= num_token_non_padded, :] = 0.0
 
 
-@torch.compile(dynamic=True, backend=get_compiler_backend())
+@_compile_unless_batch_invariant(dynamic=True, backend=get_compiler_backend())
 def _biased_grouped_topk_postprocess(
     topk_ids, expert_location_dispatch_info, num_token_non_padded
 ):

@@ -0,0 +1,69 @@
+"""In batch-invariant mode the torch.compile'd MoE routing functions run eagerly.
+
+Inductor tunes the compiled routing kernels by timing on first use, so their
+summation order, and the selected experts, can differ between server starts and
+with the batch. Deterministic inference needs the eager path.
+"""
+
+import unittest
+from unittest.mock import patch
+
+import torch
+
+import sglang.srt.layers.moe.topk as topk_module
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=5, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+ROUTING_FUNCTIONS = (
+    "grouped_topk_gpu",
+    "kimi_k2_biased_topk_impl",
+    "biased_topk_impl",
+    "biased_grouped_topk_impl",
+    "_biased_grouped_topk_postprocess",
+)
+
+
+def _compiled_must_not_run(*args, **kwargs):
+    raise AssertionError("the compiled routing function ran in batch-invariant mode")
+
+
+class TestTopkBatchInvariantEager(CustomTestCase):
+    def test_routing_functions_are_wrapped(self):
+        for name in ROUTING_FUNCTIONS:
+            with self.subTest(name=name):
+                self.assertTrue(hasattr(getattr(topk_module, name), "compiled"))
+
+    def test_batch_invariant_mode_runs_eagerly(self):
+        torch.manual_seed(0)
+        hidden_states = torch.randn(5, 16)
+        gating_output = torch.randn(5, 64)
+        fn = topk_module.grouped_topk_gpu
+        args = (hidden_states, gating_output, 6, True, 8, 3)
+
+        with (
+            patch.object(
+                topk_module, "is_batch_invariant_mode_enabled", return_value=True
+            ),
+            patch.object(fn, "compiled", _compiled_must_not_run),
+        ):
+            weights, ids = fn(*args)
+        eager_weights, eager_ids = fn.__wrapped__(*args)
+        self.assertTrue(torch.equal(weights, eager_weights))
+        self.assertTrue(torch.equal(ids, eager_ids))
+
+    def test_normal_mode_uses_the_compiled_function(self):
+        sentinel = object()
+        fn = topk_module.grouped_topk_gpu
+        with (
+            patch.object(
+                topk_module, "is_batch_invariant_mode_enabled", return_value=False
+            ),
+            patch.object(fn, "compiled", return_value=sentinel),
+        ):
+            self.assertIs(fn(torch.randn(2, 4), torch.randn(2, 8), 2, True), sentinel)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
